label: IGH / DUX4

sections.text: IGH is the immunoglobulin heavy-chain locus, with potent B-lineage regulatory elements.
DUX4 encodes a double-homeobox transcription factor normally active during early embryonic development.

Insertion or rearrangement of the repetitive DUX4 locus into IGH regulatory architecture causes abnormal DUX4 expression and a distinctive B-ALL transcriptional program, frequently with secondary ERG alterations.

DUX4-rearranged childhood B-ALL generally has favorable outcomes in reported cohorts, despite frequent IKZF1 alterations; this is a subtype-level observation rather than a conclusion from ERG deletion alone.
